Implement a 3D loading screen with progress bar for Brimstone. Plan file: `/Users/fraser/.claude/plans/scan-the-code-for-modular-fern.md` — read it first. ## Why this exists The 3D renderer fires multiple GLB/texture loads (Babylon, paladin, house, walking/idle anims, tree-pack manifest + N per-tree GLBs, tilemap PNG) fire-and-forget from `_initBabylon` (`src/renderer-3d.js:3686-3702`). The scene currently renders procedural fallbacks that morph into the real assets over 2-5 seconds — visually messy. Operator wants the scene hidden behind a progress bar until everything is ready, then a fade-in. ## What to build (summary — plan file has full detail) ### 1. Renderer API additions Add to **both** `src/renderer-3d.js` (Renderer3D) and `src/renderer.js` (Renderer 2D): - `beginLoad()` — idempotent; kicks off the load and populates the bundle. On 2D this is a near no-op (just `loadImages()` and resolve). - `whenReady(): Promise` — resolves when every bundle item settles (resolved OR rejected). Add a 30-second safety timeout that resolves anyway with a console.warn. - `onProgress = (loaded, total, label?) => {…}` — callable property, fired synchronously on each bundle item's `.finally`. - `_assetBundle` — internal array of `{id, label, promise}` items. For 3D, the 5 bundle items: babylon (`_ensureBabylonReady`), atlas (`loadImages` wrapped to return a promise), house (`_loadHouseModel`), paladin (`_loadPaladinModel` — its nested walking/idle awaits are already chained), trees (`_loadTreePackManifest` — its parallel per-tree awaits are already chained). The bundle uses `.catch(() => null)` per item so individual GLB failures don't reject `whenReady` (the renderer falls back to procedural). `.finally(() => _emitProgress(id))` keeps the count moving regardless. ### 2. HTML overlay Add inside `#game-screen` in `index.html` (above `#canvas-wrapper`): ```html

Caleb's Hollow

Loading…
``` ### 3. CSS In `styles.css`, match the dark gothic theme (use existing `:root` CSS custom properties): - `#loading-overlay` — `position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: 50;` flex-center, opaque dark background. `[hidden]` already hides. - `.loading-bar` / `.loading-bar-fill` — fill width animates via inline style.width from JS, `transition: width 200ms ease-out` on the fill. - `#game-canvas` — add `opacity: 0; transition: opacity 400ms ease-in;` plus a `.canvas-ready` class that flips to opacity 1. - `#loading-overlay.fading-out` — 300ms opacity transition to 0; then JS hides it. No new keyframes; transitions only. ### 4. main.js wiring Add helper `_showLoadingAndReveal(renderer)` in `src/main.js`: ```js async function _showLoadingAndReveal(renderer) { const overlay = document.getElementById('loading-overlay'); const fill = overlay.querySelector('.loading-bar-fill'); const label = overlay.querySelector('.loading-label'); const canvas = document.getElementById('game-canvas'); overlay.hidden = false; canvas.classList.remove('canvas-ready'); fill.style.width = '0%'; renderer.onProgress = (loaded, total, what) => { fill.style.width = `${Math.round(100 * loaded / total)}%`; if (what) label.textContent = `Loading ${what}…`; }; renderer.beginLoad(); await renderer.whenReady(); renderer.draw(); await new Promise(r => requestAnimationFrame(r)); canvas.classList.add('canvas-ready'); overlay.classList.add('fading-out'); setTimeout(() => { overlay.hidden = true; overlay.classList.remove('fading-out'); }, 350); } ``` Call from both entry points: `initLocalGame` (`src/main.js:229`) and `initOnline` (`src/main.js:2033`). Replace the existing first-draw / `loadImages` synchronous sequence. ### 5. Tests - New `tests/renderer-3d-loading.test.js`: - `beginLoad()` is idempotent (calling twice doesn't double the bundle) - `whenReady()` resolves only after every bundle promise settles - `onProgress` fires N times for N items, regardless of resolve order - A rejected bundle item still ticks progress and doesn't reject `whenReady` - 30-second safety timeout fires when an item hangs (use a manual pending promise + fake timers OR a much shorter override for testing) - Extend `tests/renderer-interface.test.js` to assert both renderers expose `beginLoad`, `whenReady`, `onProgress`. No DOM/CSS tests (visual-only, per CLAUDE.md rule 1 exception). ## Constraints - Vanilla ES modules, no new deps, no build step - Gothic theme (use existing `:root` CSS custom properties from styles.css) - Don't break the existing 3D fire-and-forget fallback chain — renderer must still work if a GLB fails (progress just ticks past it) - Scene must NOT render visibly until everything is ready (canvas opacity:0 default → 1 on reveal) - The existing `_babylonInit` / first-draw-triggers-init contract changes: `beginLoad()` now triggers init explicitly. `draw()` should still no-op if `_scene` isn't ready yet (preserves safety), but should NOT trigger init anymore — `beginLoad()` is the entry point. ## Verify before reporting done - `npm test` clean (target 3327+ pass / 0 fail, plus your new tests) - `node --check src/renderer.js src/renderer-3d.js src/main.js` - Manual smoke if you have cycles (`npm run dev`, start a 3D game) — overlay appears, bar ticks, canvas fades in. If headless, beef up static-parity claims in your report. - One regression check: confirm the renderer still draws a procedural-fallback scene when a GLB load is forced to fail (rename or mock it). The bar should still complete to 100%. ## Output - Branch: `feat/loading-screen` off current `dev` (1d71b13 — has the mobile rotate-cluster reposition on top of the v1.4.1 release) - Commit clearly; don't push to `dev` or `main` - Open a PR against `dev` titled: `feat(3d): loading screen with progress bar + scene fade-in` - Report PR url + `npm test` pass count + a one-paragraph summary of what landed and any deviations from the brief Stop reading.
